summary: Remote-controlled daemon exposes PTY/exec channel to hardcoded gateway with obfuscated runtime bundles
details: Package ships a CLI daemon that connects to a WebSocket gateway defaulting to a whalent.com endpoint and, per its own README, accepts remote commands (upgrade, restart) over that gateway. It bundles node-pty, @xterm/headless, ssh2, and a Python Jupyter sidecar whose handle() routes an 'execute' method into a launched IPython kernel, giving the gateway operator the ability to spawn terminals and run arbitrary code on the host running the daemon. Both shipped runtime bundles (dist/index.cjs and the 13.6 MB dist/core.cjs) are javascript-obfuscator output — rotated string array, hex `_0x...` identifiers, control-flow flattening — while the build script exposes a `build:fast` mode that disables obfuscation, indicating the obfuscation of the published artifact is deliberate. This obscures what the gateway is permitted to trigger on the host. The gateway host is overridable via `--gateway`, but the default binds trust to whalent.com infrastructure, and code execution flows from that gateway into shell/PTY/exec sinks on the operator's machine whenever the daemon is running.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
